title: Orbit AI is now in Beta: your campus assistant, reimagined
excerpt: A first look at how Orbit helps students find deals, plan spending, and get quick answers — right inside the app.
cover_image_alt: Three students on a sunlit campus bench, leaning in to look at something on one of their phones
intro: Orbit is StudentVerse's new AI companion — built for campus life, not generic chat. In this beta we are testing how it finds deals, explains spending, and answers quick questions without leaving the app. This guide walks through what Orbit can do today, what is still learning, and how to get the most out of it.

sections.heading: WHAT ORBIT IS (AND ISN'T)
sections.content: Orbit is a campus-tuned assistant, not a search engine. It knows StudentVerse partners, your saved preferences, and common student workflows — so it can answer 'where can I print near AUD for under AED 5' in one go.

blocks.text: Orbit is a campus-tuned assistant, not a search engine. It knows StudentVerse partners, your saved preferences, and common student workflows — so it can answer 'where can I print near AUD for under AED 5' in one go.

Remembers your campus and preferences
Answers in one go, not a list of links
Not a generic web search — campus-first

blocks.text: Ask in plain language — 'cheap cafe near DSO with student discount' — and Orbit surfaces the best match, opening hours, and how to redeem. No filters to fiddle with.

title: How UAE students are actually spending their budgets in 2026
excerpt: We looked at real usage data to see where student money goes each month.
cover_image_alt: Two students at a library table working out a monthly budget with a phone, a notebook and a stack of receipts
intro: We anonymised six months of StudentVerse spend data to see where money really goes — rent, food, transport, printing, and the small daily taps that add up. The pattern is surprisingly consistent across Dubai campuses, and it points to three easy wins for the next semester.

sections.heading: THE BIG PICTURE
sections.content: On average students spend AED 2,800–3,400 a month. Food is the swing factor — cooking twice a week cuts it by 18% versus eating out daily.

blocks.text: On average students spend AED 2,800–3,400 a month. Food is the swing factor — cooking twice a week cuts it by 18% versus eating out daily.

items: Average: AED 2,800–3,400 per month
Food is the largest swing factor
Cooking twice a week saves ~18%
Small daily taps add up faster than rent

sections.heading: FOOD & GROCERIES
sections.content: Groceries are 31% of spend, cafes another 12%. Batch-cooking Sundays and using the AUD co-op discount were the two most common savers.

blocks.text: Groceries are 31% of spend, cafes another 12%. Batch-cooking Sundays and using the AUD co-op discount were the two most common savers.

blocks.title: QUICK TIP
blocks.text: Shop the co-op on Sunday and batch-cook two meals — the data shows this one habit saves ~AED 220/month.

sections.heading: TRANSPORT
sections.content: Metro + NOL is still cheapest. Students who mixed in one weekly taxi averaged AED 210 more than those who didn't — the single biggest avoidable cost.

blocks.text: Metro + NOL is still cheapest. Students who mixed in one weekly taxi averaged AED 210 more than those who didn't — the single biggest avoidable cost.

items: Metro + NOL is consistently cheapest
One weekly taxi adds ~AED 210/month
Preload NOL on payday to avoid top-up fees
Check shuttle times before booking a flat

sections.heading: PRINTING & SUPPLIES
sections.content: Exam months spike printing by 3×. Booking through the campus hub rather than mall counters saved an average AED 38 per exam season.

blocks.text: Exam months spike printing by 3×. Booking through the campus hub rather than mall counters saved an average AED 38 per exam season.

blocks.text: We found 42% of students pay for two music apps at once. Audit your subscriptions once a semester — it is the fastest AED 30–60 back.

title: Baitna pilot launches: student housing, simplified
excerpt: An early look at our new housing arm, currently piloting with select universities.
cover_image_alt: Three students unpacking boxes into a sunlit student apartment on move-in day
intro: Baitna is our answer to scattered listings, WhatsApp brokers, and unclear contracts. For this pilot we have verified 120 rooms across Dubai South, Al Barsha and International City — all with clear pricing, photos, and a StudentVerse guarantee. Here is how it works if your university is in the pilot.

sections.heading: HOW THE PILOT WORKS
sections.content: You browse verified listings in the app, book a viewing, and sign a single bilingual contract. No broker fee — StudentVerse handles the match.

blocks.text: You browse verified listings in the app, book a viewing, and sign a single bilingual contract. No broker fee — StudentVerse handles the match.

Book a viewing in one tap

sections.heading: 7. LEARN THE LOCAL RULES
sections.content: Dubai is highly international, but UAE laws and public expectations still apply. Do not assume that conduct accepted in another country is automatically legal in Dubai.

blocks.text: Dubai is highly international, but UAE laws and public expectations still apply. Do not assume that conduct accepted in another country is automatically legal in Dubai.

items: Only consume alcohol in licensed settings and follow age requirements
Never possess or use illegal drugs
Avoid aggressive, abusive or offensive behaviour
Respect privacy when filming or photographing others
Be careful about what you post publicly online
Carry identification where appropriate

blocks.title: QUICK TIP
blocks.text: When unsure, check an official UAE or Dubai Government source rather than relying on social-media comments.
